llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Windows print and document-processing helper, with some sensitive capabilities users should intentionally control.

dimensions.detail: The Windows-only environment, printer configuration, LibreOffice conversion, SumatraPDF printing, and local document libraries fit the stated print/document workflow.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses winget to install SumatraPDF and LibreOffice, pip installs requirements, detects printers, and writes a local printer config; these actions are documented, but dependencies are not pinned or hash-verified.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Natural-language routing is broad and CLAUDE.md allows direct printing without confirmation when understood; this is purpose-aligned but users should prefer preview or confirmation for shared printers, sensitive files, and destructive edits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no service, scheduled task, startup hook, credential harvesting, remote payload execution, or exfiltration behavior; persistence is limited to installed dependencies/applications and local printer configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe printing plus PDF manipulation, Office editing, and optional Adobe photo workflows; PDF decrypt and Office modification are sensitive but disclosed in SKILL.md, README.md, and routing notes.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a local Windows skill that can send files to a physical printer, create modified copies of documents, remove PDF passwords when you provide them, and install third-party software and Python packages. Use preview/confirmation for sensitive documents or shared printers, and prefer pinned dependencies or a virtual environment before running setup.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The scanner's mismatch concern is downgraded because the package openly routes PDF tools, Office editing, image handling, and printing in user-facing artifacts, although the top-level name emphasizes printing.
[SDI-1] expected: Broad PDF and Office manipulation is more than raw printing, but it is documented as part of preparing and modifying files for print-oriented workflows.
[SDI-2] expected: PDF encryption/decryption is disclosed and requires a password for decryption; users should treat decrypted outputs as sensitive local copies.
[SQP-2] expected: Direct printing and document modifications are real side effects, but they are visible parts of the workflow; preview or explicit confirmation is advisable for sensitive or ambiguous requests.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Automatic translation of unsupported languages can change intent and should not be relied on for print settings or file edits without showing the interpreted request back to the user.
[LP3] expected: The skill relies on shell-based installation and local command execution because it integrates with Windows printing tools, though a tighter permission model would improve clarity.
[AST4] expected: Subprocess calls invoke LibreOffice and SumatraPDF with explicit argument lists and shell=False by default, so the command-injection concern is reduced.
[SC1] unexpected: The requirements use lower-bound dependency versions without a lockfile or hashes, creating dependency drift and supply-chain risk.
[T08] unexpected: The SARIF dependency finding is supported by requirements.txt and setup.ps1, but there is no artifact evidence of malicious package names or deliberate remote payload behavior.
